items.followUp: How are the results of an experiment presented and used to reach a conclusion?

rubric.why: Award for explaining how results are organized or presented.
rubric.description: Results are organized or presented clearly, for example in tables or graphs.
rubric.how: Look for a reference to data/results and a suitable method of presentation; accept any correct example such as a table or graph.

rubric.why: Award for explaining that results are interpreted to reach a conclusion about the hypothesis.
rubric.description: The biologist interprets the results and draws a conclusion to support or reject the hypothesis.
rubric.how: Look for a conclusion linked to the hypothesis, including whether it is supported or rejected.

modelAnswer: A biologist organizes the experimental data, often in tables or graphs.
The biologist interprets the results and draws a conclusion to support or reject the hypothesis.

items.followUp: Define a species and list the taxonomic categories from species to kingdom.

rubric.why: A taxon is any recognized classification group.
rubric.description: A taxon is a group or category of organisms at any level of classification.
rubric.how: Award for defining a taxon as a classification group or category.

rubric.why: A taxonomic hierarchy is an ordered arrangement of taxonomic categories.
rubric.description: A taxonomic hierarchy is the arrangement of taxonomic categories in a ranked sequence.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the categories are arranged in an order or sequence.

modelAnswer: A taxon is a group of organisms at any level of classification.
A taxonomic hierarchy is the arrangement of taxonomic categories in a ranked sequence.

items.followUp: State two characteristics of kingdom Fungi.

rubric.why: Award for one correct characteristic of plants.
rubric.description: Plants are multicellular and eukaryotic; their cells have cellulose walls and chloroplasts with chlorophyll, and most make food by photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award for any one distinct, correct characteristic of kingdom Plantae.

rubric.why: Award for a second correct characteristic of plants.
rubric.description: Plants are multicellular and eukaryotic; their cells have cellulose walls and chloroplasts with chlorophyll, and most make food by photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award for a second distinct, correct characteristic of kingdom Plantae.

modelAnswer: Kingdom Plantae consists of multicellular eukaryotic organisms.
Their cells have cellulose cell walls and chloroplasts containing chlorophyll for photosynthesis.

items.followUp: State two differences between plant cells and animal cells.

rubric.why: Award for a correct feature of the primary wall.
rubric.description: The primary wall is the first wall formed and is relatively thin and flexible, allowing cell growth.
rubric.how: Look for a correct primary-wall feature, such as being first formed, thin, flexible, or allowing growth.

rubric.why: Award for a correct contrast about the secondary wall.
rubric.description: The secondary wall is deposited inside the primary wall after cell growth and is usually thicker and more rigid.
rubric.how: Look for a correct secondary-wall feature and its contrast with the primary wall.

modelAnswer: The primary wall is formed first; it is thin and flexible, allowing the cell to grow.
The secondary wall is deposited inside the primary wall after growth; it is thicker and more rigid, often due to lignin.

items.followUp: State two functions of rough endoplasmic reticulum.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the smooth ER's role in lipid or steroid synthesis.
rubric.description: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum synthesizes lipids, including steroid hormones.
rubric.how: Look for lipid or steroid synthesis.

rubric.why: Award for a second correct function of smooth ER.
rubric.description: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum helps detoxify drugs and poisons; it can also store calcium ions or take part in carbohydrate metabolism.
rubric.how: Award for any one additional correct function, distinct from lipid synthesis.

modelAnswer: Smooth endoplasmic reticulum synthesizes lipids, including steroid hormones.
It helps detoxify drugs and poisons.

items.followUp: What is metastasis, and which type of tumour can undergo it?

rubric.why: Award for describing the defining behaviour of benign tumours.
rubric.description: Benign tumours are non-cancerous and remain localized; they do not spread to other parts of the body.
rubric.how: Look for non-cancerous/localized behaviour or an equivalent statement that benign tumours do not spread.

rubric.why: Award for describing the defining behaviour of malignant tumours.
rubric.description: Malignant tumours are cancerous, invade nearby tissues, and can spread to other parts of the body.
rubric.how: Look for cancerous or invasive behaviour, especially spread to other body parts.

modelAnswer: Benign tumours are non-cancerous and remain localized; they do not spread to other parts of the body.
Malignant tumours are cancerous, invade nearby tissues, and may spread to other parts of the body.

items.followUp: What is a cell plate, and how does it form during plant-cell cytokinesis?

rubric.why: Award for identifying the phragmoplast and its location during division.
rubric.description: The phragmoplast is an arrangement of microtubules and vesicles that forms between the daughter nuclei in a dividing plant cell.
rubric.how: Look for the microtubule/vesicle structure or its position between daughter nuclei.

rubric.why: Award for stating the phragmoplast's role in cell-plate formation.
rubric.description: The phragmoplast guides vesicles that join to form the cell plate during cytokinesis.
rubric.how: Look for the cell plate and a correct link to its formation or guidance by the phragmoplast.

modelAnswer: The phragmoplast is an arrangement of microtubules and vesicles that forms between the daughter nuclei in a dividing plant cell.
It guides vesicles to join and form the cell plate during cytokinesis.

items.followUp: What is a substrate, and how does it interact with an enzyme?

rubric.why: Award for defining an enzyme as a biological catalyst that speeds up reactions.
rubric.description: An enzyme is a biological catalyst that speeds up biochemical reactions.
rubric.how: Look for both the catalyst role and the speeding up of biochemical reactions.

rubric.why: Award for stating that enzymes are not used up in the reaction.
rubric.description: An enzyme is not consumed during the reaction and can be used again.
rubric.how: Look for the idea that the enzyme remains unchanged or is not consumed.

modelAnswer: An enzyme is a biological catalyst that speeds up biochemical reactions.
It is not consumed during the reaction and can be used again.
